stemBlocks.value: Use the grid to solve x + 2y = 10 and 3x − y = 5 graphically, giving the solution correct to 1 decimal place. (a) Draw both lines. (b) State the solution correct to 1 decimal place.
Think first: Both equations need rearranging into y = mx + c before anything can be plotted.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p136-q07 from workbook page 136.

contentBlocks.value: 2y = 10 − x, then divide every term by 2
Result: Three points for each line

solutionSteps.instruction: Plot both lines and read where they cross.

contentBlocks.value: The crossing point is a little under x = 3, a little over y = 3.5

strategyBlocks.value: Make y the subject of each equation, plot three points for each line, read the crossing point off the grid and confirm it by solving algebraically.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) Both lines drawn on the grid  (b) x = 2.9, y = 3.6 (to 1 decimal place).

whyThisWorks.value: Two straight lines with different gradients meet at exactly one point, and that point is the only pair of values satisfying both equations. Because the true solution here is x = 20/7, it does not sit on a gridline, so the graph gives an estimate that rounding to 1 decimal place makes honest. Checking algebraically shows how close a careful reading should be.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting to halve the 10 as well as the x when rearranging 2y = 10 − x.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Forgetting to halve the 10 as well as the x when rearranging 2y = 10 − x.
